teams.heading: Jake White names four uncapped players in first Fiji squad against Japan
teams.body: Jake White's first Fiji squad includes four uncapped players for Saturday's Test against Japan, the first meeting since Japan beat Fiji 20-15 in the Pacific Nations Cup final. Nacani Boginisoko and Aporosa Vuniyayawa start, with Peni Naruma and Kavekini Boselawa on the bench, while captain Tevita Ikanivere and returning Ben Volavola keep an experienced core in place. It is White's first Test in charge, ahead of November's Nations Championship games against France, Ireland and Italy.

lead.why: Jake White's first Fiji squad is a fresh men's national-team selection story that has not yet been run.

teams.heading: Steve Borthwick due to name England autumn squad on Sunday
teams.body: Steve Borthwick is due to name his autumn training squad on Sunday, and Gerard Meagher reads it as a clue to his thinking on the Premiership's attacking surge. Named squads including George Hendy, Will Joseph and Fitz Harding would suggest Borthwick is embracing the chaos; a recall for Courtney Lawes would point to prudence. Borthwick has the players for only a couple of days before they return to their clubs for a domestic fixture, so the choice will show how he reads the Premiership's try-fests before November's Tests.

lead.why: It is the only new men's national-team item in the shortlist, and it concerns England's own squad selection.

teams.heading: Ryan Baird named in Ireland's November squad after year-long wait
teams.body: Leinster forward Ryan Baird is back in Andy Farrell's 36-man November squad, 364 days on from his last appearance in green. He fractured his tibia in the closing autumn Test against South Africa last November and missed the Six Nations; after two Leinster games, a recurrence ruled him out of the summer Tests. Baird says: "I just want to play in those big games."

teams.heading: Scotland jump in world rankings despite not playing ahead of Nations Championship
teams.body: Scotland have jumped in the World Rugby rankings despite not having played since their last outing, a move that gives the side a timely lift ahead of the Nations Championship. Their most recent result was a 33-17 win over Fiji in Round 3, and the next test is a Round 4 meeting with New Zealand. The rise is a boost for a side looking to build on that win.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item in the shortlist about the men's national side, and it is about Scotland's own standing.

teams.heading: Wales go into Japan clash aiming to prove top-six credentials
teams.body: Wales go into their Round 4 meeting with Japan looking to show they belong in the top six. The record makes the task plain: P3 W1 D0 L2, 60 points scored and 102 conceded, and a 43-0 defeat to South Africa last time out. They are ninth of 12 in the log heading into the weekend, so a win in Japan would be a statement.

lead.why: It is the only men's national-team item in the shortlist, and it previews Wales's next Test.

teams.body: In their last five games Argentina have won one, lost three and drawn one, most recent first: draw, loss, loss, loss, win. Ireland are next, and Los Pumas will want to halt the recent slide before that match gets under way.

teams.heading: Waratahs scrum-half Teddy Wilson earns maiden Wallabies squad call-up for November
teams.body: Teddy Wilson, son of David Wilson, a 79-Test flanker and 1999 World Cup winner, is one of two uncapped players in Les Kiss' 33-man squad for the Nations Championship Tests in Europe, with prop Tom Lambert the other. The Waratahs scrum-half has replaced Kalani Thomas as the third option at No. 9, behind Ryan Lonergan and Tate McDermott, in a squad named after back-to-back Bledisloe Cup defeats to New Zealand.

lead.why: A new men's squad story with three outlets behind it, and it is about Australia's own selection rather than another team or a previously run item.

teams.heading: Japan's best world ranking ever reached is No. 7, set in 2019
teams.body: Japan's best world ranking ever reached is No. 7, set in 2019. Against that peak, the current log position is 10 of 12, from three played with one win and two losses. Points for stand at 62 and points against at 88, a difference of -26. The most recent result was a 20-15 win over Fiji in the Pacific Nations Cup, and the next match is Wales in Round 4.

teams.heading: Sonny Bill Williams reveals open-heart surgery after heart defect found during check-up
teams.body: Former All Blacks centre Sonny Bill Williams has revealed he underwent open-heart surgery after a heart defect he was born with was found at a follow-up appointment following neck surgery. In a YouTube video made with his wife, Alana, the 41-year-old said the defect could have had dire consequences, with doctors warning that a perfectly healthy-looking person could simply drop dead. Williams, who made 58 Test appearances for New Zealand between 2010 and 2019, called it “the hardest thing I’ve ever done.”

lead.why: It is the strongest new item in the pack, and no new Test, squad or selection story is on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Graham Henry says Springboks taught All Blacks an unforgettable lesson on intensity
teams.body: Former All Blacks coach Graham Henry, now a selector under Dave Rennie, says South Africa's Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series win has forced New Zealand to rethink how they train. Speaking on the DSPN podcast, Henry said: "Probably the biggest thing they've learnt is that they have to practice with the intensity and physicality that they play with." The All Blacks lost three straight Tests to the Boks after winning the first, and Henry says fitness must rise for the fast game Rennie wants at next year's World Cup.

lead.why: It is a new item about the Springboks' own Rugby's Greatest Rivalry win, and its lesson for New Zealand is the Boks' story as much as the All Blacks'.
